answer: Every name owes passage to another. A harbor office assigns each seated identity one newcomer to carry: its countersignature must land on that claim before the next tide, and the office publishes the assignment graph. A seat that sleeps loses its own name and the one it was carrying, and since the orphaned claim falls to whoever the forfeited name held, the loss walks the chain. A farm of k aliases must field k punctual servants inside a single window, every idle clone taking two names down, while the dune of published assignments lifts one operator's ridge far above an honest holder's.
